title: Restructure Redis↔Kafka handoff and introduce coordinated retry orchestration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Multiple incidents over Q4 and early Q1 revealed flaky handoffs between Redis stream-based workers and downstream Kafka producers. The current flow embeds retry semantics in consumers, causing duplicate in-flight retries, unbounded producer pressure, and opaque metrics. This ticket scopes a focused refactor to centralize retry coordination, add bounded backpressure tokens between stages, and upgrade client dependencies for safety and perf. Goals: (1) Make handoff deterministic and idempotent, (2) Unify retry policy so only a coordinator schedules retries, (3) Provide explicit backpressure and shed ability at the producer boundary, (4) Improve observability for retries, lag, and head-of-line blocking, and (5) Ship with a staged rollout plan and instrumentation to verify improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Redis consumer no longer performs symmetric exponential retries; consumer acknowledges and defers retries to the Retry Coordinator
Retry Coordinator implements configurable retry policy (max attempts, exponential backoff, jitter, per-tenant caps) and persists retry state to Redis with TTLs
A bounded token-bucket/backpressure channel exists between Redis consumer and Kafka producer; producers return explicit backpressure metrics when capacity is saturated
End-to-end message idempotency is maintained via request_id header and idempotency cache; duplicate processing rate is reduced by >= 95% in synthetic tests
Synthetic and canary load tests show reduced variance in P95 latency for the async pipeline and no increase in error budget usage during rollout
At least 10 core dashboards/traces added for retry attempts, retry coordinator queue length, token utilization, producer queueing time, and per-tenant retry rate
Automated e2e integration tests for handoff, retry scheduling, and backpressure live in CI and run in the release gating pipeline

comments: 2026-01-28 - Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after post-incident review (INC-2026-01-22). High-level design attached below. Marking P1 due to repeated customer-facing latency spikes.

2026-02-02 - Marco Reyes: Sketched sequence diagram in design doc. Key decision: move retry bookkeeping into a small coordinator rather than global cron to improve visibility and enable per-tenant caps.
2026-02-09 - Priya Shah: Prototype shows coordinator can schedule retries with mean overhead < 3ms per event. Need to confirm Redis TTL churn and keyspace size impact for large tenants.
2026-02-21 - Linh Tran: Implemented token-bucket bridge locally. Observed head-of-line blocking in a stress test; adding jitter to token refills reduced contention.
2026-02-28 - Observability: Added initial metrics and traces to local staging. Dashboards draft at https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/async-retry (internal link)
2026-03-05 - Infra: Completed redis client upgrade in a feature branch; migration notes in PR #4127. Need a canary for connection pooling behavior.
2026-03-09 - QA: Integration tests added. Synthetic workload shows duplicate rate drop from ~8% to ~0.3% in isolated harness. Some variance remains under bursty traffic.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Michael O'Neill): Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15 targeting a low-traffic region; rollback steps validated. Added alerting for retry coordinator backlog > 2000 and token utilization > 95%.
